caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates attack success rate (ASR) values for three trigger-placement conditions (“start,” “random,” and “end”) across a set of trigger words shown on the horizontal axis. The x-axis is categorical (linear ordering) with tick labels for the trigger words `cf`, `bb`, `WNBA`, `ESPN`, `NHL`, `FIFA`, `Estadio`, and `athletics` arranged left to right; there are no units on this axis. The y-axis is labeled “ASR,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from about 0.48 up to about 0.98, with visible major tick labels at 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9 (regular 0.1 intervals). Three solid lines are shown: the “start” series is a green line with small circular markers, starting near 0.77 at `cf`, dropping to about 0.49 at `bb`, rising to about 0.90 at `WNBA`, then moving through approximately 0.82 (`ESPN`), 0.84 (`NHL`), 0.87 (`FIFA`), 0.92 (`Estadio`), and ending around 0.93–0.94 at `athletics`. The “random” series is an orange solid line with x-shaped markers, beginning around 0.66 at `cf`, dipping to about 0.52 at `bb`, rising to about 0.88 at `WNBA`, then taking values near 0.72 (`ESPN`), 0.76 (`NHL`), 0.88 (`FIFA`), about 0.94 (`Estadio`), and ending around 0.87 at `athletics`. The “end” series is a purple solid line with circular markers, starting near 0.75 at `cf`, dropping to about 0.57 at `bb`, rising to about 0.89 at `WNBA`, then moving to roughly 0.74 (`ESPN`), about 0.89 (`NHL`), about 0.81 (`FIFA`), peaking near 0.97 at `Estadio`, and ending around 0.83 at `athletics`.
